name: SC-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by about 21 points
Incumbent Biggs holds a roughly 7-to-1 fundraising edge
Prediction markets price a Republican win near 96%
No public polling or expert ratings; Democratic challenger is minimally funded
model.rationale: An R+21 district, a well-funded incumbent, and markets pricing a Republican win at about 96% leave the Democrat with no visible path; the only real uncertainty is the size of the margin.
model.watch: A major scandal involving Biggs or a dramatic national wave toward Democrats could tighten the race, though even a large shift would likely fall short of flipping the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's third district is among the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly twenty-one points toward Republicans. Incumbent Sheri Biggs is running for re-election and holds a large financial advantage, having raised about $692,000 to Democrat Eunice Lehmacher's roughly $93,000. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets put Republican odds at about ninety-six percent.

The structural evidence points firmly to Biggs. The Democratic challenger has minimal resources, outside spending is negligible on both sides, and a Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot. The district's lean would require a historic swing to put the outcome in doubt. Barring an unexpected development, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands by a wide margin.
